DriverDNA — UI v3 “cockpit feel” + U7 mobile

SPEC.md A35/A36, docs/UI-V3-PLAN.md Track A. Unlike the v2 mockup (docs/ui-redesign-mockup.html, hand-authored placeholder markup reviewed before the v2 build started), this one is assembled from real Playwright screenshots of the actual built SPA, driven by a synthetic dated 25-lap history so the score-history chart (A4) has real data to draw — because the real build already exists and passed every trust gate, showing the real thing is more honest than re-approximating it by hand.

1. Chrome-accent candidates (owner decision needed)

SPEC.md A35: a new chrome-only accent may be added, legal on the wordmark, active-tab underline, hover/press states, disclosure chevrons, and empty-state ribbons — illegal on any figure, bar, chart series, tile value, or finding row (that rule is unaffected by which hue wins). The actual build below uses cyan (#3FC7DE); magenta (#D162C2) is the documented alternative from the same two free hue regions (~185° / ~325°) — every other hue in the palette is already spoken for by a semantic meaning or the existing interaction accent.

Recommendation: cyan. It reads closer to the existing --accent steel-blue (~207°) as a family — both cool, both legible against the dark base — so the new “personality” accent feels like a sibling to the existing interaction accent rather than a competing signal. Magenta is warmer and reads more decisively as a distinct third color, which risks being mistaken for a fourth semantic hue at a glance despite never being used on a measurement. Either is compliant with A35; this is a taste call for the owner.

2. Driver home — wide layout, real sync data

≥64rem: tiles/rollup pair with the Sync panel as two columns (SPEC.md A35 “use of space”) instead of one narrow stacked column.

4. Methodology disclosure, open

A3: the "how is this measured?" arrow, engine-sourced text (GET /api/explain), never hand-written per view.

5. Score history — the manipulable line graph

A4: Driver Model fundamental scores over time (dm-hist-v1), on a synthetic 25-dated-lap driver so every bucket has real evidence (the shared test fixture is deliberately undated, so this is the one screenshot here the trust gates themselves never exercise in a real browser — tests/test_score_history_ui.py covers that populated path directly, on its own throwaway DB).
